Folks — draft answers below, put together after a quick pass with legal. I'll incorporate Karthik's provenance bits once he sends checksums. This is aimed at the procurement template fields.

--- Licensing (short summary for spreadsheet) ---
- Our public catalog contains a mix of open-source and Redwood-curated variants. Typical open-model licenses we encounter and ship as-is: Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD-3-Clause. Where models are released under Creative Commons for outputs, we note the CC variant (e.g., CC-BY-4.0).
- We do not relicense upstream model weights; we surface the upstream license in the catalog entry. For models where the upstream license prohibits commercial use, we flag "restricted" in the license column and provide alternatives where available.
- For Redwood's proprietary variants (fine-tuned or quantized variants that include Redwood optimizations), we ship under Redwood Inference terms; redistribution of those binaries is restricted. We call this out per-model in the catalog UI and API.
- Tokenizers and small helper libraries follow the license of their original upstream package (listed in each model's metadata).

--- Provenance & verifiability ---
- Each catalog entry includes a model card with: upstream source link, training date, upstream checkpoint id (when available), dataset descriptors, and a SHA256 checksum of the weights artifact we serve.
- For models we host (weights stored by Redwood), we publish checksums and a signed provenance blob (PGP-signed manifest) accessible from the model card URL. Customers can verify artifact integrity and origin.
- For community models we proxy, we record the original source URI and a capture timestamp; when upstream updates, we snapshot and surface both versions.

--- Version pinning & update policy ---
- Customers can pin models via the API/console by setting model=redwood/<model-name>@<version-hash>. Pinned versions remain immutable for the duration of the customer's deployment unless they opt in to auto-update.
- Update types: security hotfix, performance improvement, and non-breaking enhancements. We classify updates and expose a changelog per model.
- Deprecation policy: once a model is scheduled for deprecation we give customers 90 days notice for standard releases and 30 days for critical security fixes (with backport options for enterprise Dedicated/Private customers).
- For Dedicated/Private customers we support customer-managed model uploads and full on-prem version-locking; Redwood will not auto-replace customer-managed artifacts without explicit consent.

--- Delivery & evidence ---
- Attached: redwood_model_catalog_export_20260504.jsonl (machine-readable snapshot) and a short PDF summary I'll produce when Karthik and Connor confirm provenance and pinning language.

Marissa
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_model_catalog_export_20260504.jsonl]

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFP: Model catalog licensing & provenance questionnaire (provenance details)

Adding the provenance/checksum details and our verification process — paste these into the spreadsheet under section 3: Provenance & lineage.

Provenance details to include:
- For each hosted artifact we publish: exact upstream URI, captured-at timestamp, storage location (s3://redwood-models/<model>/<version>), and SHA256 checksum of the artifact we serve.
- Checksum signing: we sign manifest files with our release key and publish the key fingerprint in the model card. Example: key fingerprint = AB3C:9F2D:... (we'll provide the full fingerprint in the spreadsheet).
- Reproducibility notes: where feasible, we include training hyperparams, tokenizer version, and dockerized inference environment hashes. For models where upstream data is restricted, we provide dataset descriptors without exposing raw data.
- Audit trail: all catalog imports and updates are logged with user, timestamp, and source commit (internal audit logs, available to enterprise customers on request for Dedicated/Private).

I'll attach a small CSV of checksums for the top-20 models. Let me know if procurement needs signed manifests for every artifact — we can generate per-request but it will add time.

Karthik
Applied ML, Redwood Inference

Hi Sara / Tom,

Thanks for the RFP template. Please find our responses attached (short executive summary + completed spreadsheet): 20260504-Redwood_ModelCatalog_RFP_Responses.pdf. Key highlights:
- Licensing: catalog rows explicitly list the upstream license for each model artifact. Where we provide Redwood-curated or proprietary variants, we clearly label redistribution restrictions and offer alternative open models where downstream licensing would be an issue.
- Provenance: model cards include upstream link, capture timestamp, SHA256 checksums, and a signed provenance manifest for hosted artifacts. We can provide per-artifact signed manifests on request.
- Versioning: API and Console support immutable version pins (model@version-hash). Auto-update is opt-in; deprecation windows and changelogs are published. Dedicated/Private customers may elect to manage model artifacts entirely on their own.

Next steps: would you like a 30-min technical walk-through next week (I can include Karthik and Marissa for detailed Q&A)? If so, propose two time slots and we'll confirm.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
